**The meaning of the verse**
﴿وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ ۚ ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ﴾ ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ﴾

The good deed of those who believed in Allah, kept straight on His law and were kind to His creation is not equal to the evil deed of those who disbelieved in Him, went against His command and wronged His creation. Repel, O Messenger, whoever wrongs you with your forgiveness, forbearance and kindness, and meet his wrong to you with kindness to him; in this way the one who wronged you, with whom there was enmity, becomes like a loving supporter of yours and a close relative who cares for you. And none are granted this praiseworthy quality except those who were patient in hardships and harm and made themselves do what Allah loves; and none are granted it except one who has a great share of happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Uncle Sultan do when he found the goats in his garden? And why did he not complain about Mar'i to people, as they told him to?
2. What did Mar'i use to think every time he saw Uncle Sultan mending the fence? And when did his heart change?
3. Does repelling evil with what is better mean always keeping quiet about our rights? (No; a person may ask for his right politely and gently, and if a child is afraid of being hurt, they tell the grown-ups. But forgiveness and kindness are better, and through them enmity turns into affection.)

**This week's exercise**
Your child chooses someone who has annoyed them a little, a brother, sister or classmate, and this week answers them with one deliberate act of kindness: some help, a small gift, or a kind word. At the end of the week, talk together about what has changed between them.
